title: Career Roadmap: Security Analyst
summary: A Security Analyst protects computer systems, networks, applications, and organisational data from cyber threats. The role involves monitoring security alerts, investigating suspicious activity, analysing logs, supporting incident response, and helping organisations strengthen their security controls.

blocks.text: For students pursuing a B.Sc. in Cyber Security or Digital Forensics, this career offers a pathway into security operations, cyber incident investigation, threat intelligence, and digital evidence analysis.

rows.text: 3 years; some institutions offer a 4-year honours or research programme
Security operations centres, IT companies, banks, consulting firms, government organisations, and managed security providers
Networking, operating systems, cybersecurity, incident response, and digital forensics
Wireshark, SIEM platforms, Linux, Windows event logs, and Python
Analytical thinking, attention to detail, problem-solving, ethical judgement, and clear documentation
SOC Analyst L1, Junior Security Analyst, Security Monitoring Analyst, and Digital Forensics Intern

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Security Analyst is a broad job title. Employers may specialise in monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, cloud security, or digital forensics. Eligibility depends on the actual job description, qualifications, and practical skills.

sections.heading: What does a Security Analyst do?

blocks.text: Security monitoring
Review alerts from security information and event management (SIEM) platforms, endpoint security systems, and network monitoring tools.
Threat investigation
Investigate suspicious logins, phishing reports, unusual network connections, and potentially compromised accounts.
Incident response
Document findings, preserve relevant evidence, escalate incidents, and support authorised containment and recovery activities.
Digital forensics
Examine file-system artefacts, metadata, and event timelines while maintaining evidence integrity and chain-of-custody records.
Security improvement
Help identify vulnerabilities, document risks, track remediation, and improve organisational security procedures.
SOC Analyst
Monitors alerts, investigates security events, and escalates suspected incidents. This is a practical entry-level target for many graduates.
Digital Forensics Analyst
Examines digital evidence, reconstructs event timelines, and prepares technical investigation reports.
Threat Intelligence Analyst
Analyses threat reports, indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging cyber risks.
Vulnerability Management Analyst
Helps assess authorised vulnerability scans, prioritise remediation, and verify that security weaknesses have been addressed.
Cloud Security Analyst
Investigates cloud access events, identity permissions, security configurations, and cloud audit logs.
Other career options include incident response, security engineering, governance and compliance, identity and access management, and application security.
This plan assumes a three-year B.Sc. programme.
Year 1
Foundation
Learn computing fundamentals

items.text: Computer architecture, operating systems, and file systems.

blocks.label: Networking
blocks.text: TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, ports, routing, and firewalls.

items.text: Linux command line and Windows administration.
Python fundamentals and basic scripting.

blocks.label: Security principles
blocks.text: confidentiality, integrity, availability, and access control.

items.text: Git and basic virtual-machine setup.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Networking notes, a Linux command reference, and a basic security-log analysis project.
Year 2
Security skills
Develop investigation skills

items.text: Study malware concepts, phishing, authentication attacks, and privilege misuse.
Analyse Windows and Linux logs.
Practise network packet analysis with Wireshark.
Learn SIEM concepts, log searches, event correlation, and alert triage.
Understand vulnerability management, patching, and endpoint protection.
Learn digital evidence handling, hashing, and chain of custody.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: A simulated SOC investigation, packet-capture analysis, and incident report.
Year 3
Employability
Prepare for internships and graduate roles

items.text: Practise security alert triage and incident documentation.
Learn threat intelligence and MITRE ATT&CK fundamentals.
Use Python to parse logs and automate basic reporting.
Complete a security monitoring or digital forensics capstone.
Apply for SOC, incident response, and digital forensics internships.
Prepare a technical resume and practise security interview questions.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Three documented security projects, a portfolio, and a targeted application plan.

blocks.label: Optional fourth year
blocks.text: Use an honours or research year for advanced SIEM detections, cloud security, threat hunting, an extended internship, or a supervised digital forensics dissertation.

sections.heading: Technical and professional skills to master

rows.text: TCP/IP, DNS, ports, HTTP/S, routing, firewalls
Linux, Windows, permissions, processes, event logs
Authentication, access control, encryption concepts, patching
SIEM, log analysis, alert triage, event correlation
File systems, metadata, hashing, timelines, chain of custody
Python, regular expressions, log parsing, simple automation
Phishing, malware behaviour, indicators of compromise
Asset inventories, vulnerability prioritisation, security policies
Incident reports, technical explanations, clear escalation notes

Inspect permitted packet captures and understand network protocols and traffic patterns.

Documentation

Training resources

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Security Log Analysis
Beginner · Year 1
Analyse sample authentication logs to identify repeated failed logins, unusual login times, and unexpected account activity.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Python, Excel, sample Windows or Linux logs.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Pattern recognition, log interpretation, and reporting.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Network Traffic Investigation
Intermediate · Year 2
Examine an authorised sample packet capture, identify protocols and endpoints, and document unusual traffic patterns with supporting evidence.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Wireshark and training PCAP files.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Networking, packet analysis, and evidence-based reasoning.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Mini Security Operations Centre
Intermediate · Year 2–3
Set up a lab using synthetic or test-system logs, create detection rules, and document alert severity, investigation steps, and escalation criteria.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Wazuh or another suitable educational SIEM.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Monitoring, triage, detection, and incident documentation.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Digital Forensics Case Study
Advanced · Year 3
Examine an authorised forensic training image, calculate hashes, inspect file-system artefacts, construct a timeline, and prepare a structured report.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Autopsy and hashing utilities.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Evidence integrity, investigation methodology, and technical reporting.

For each project, publish a README describing the objective, authorised data source, lab setup, methodology, findings, limitations, and recommendations. Never upload confidential logs, credentials, or personal information.

blocks.text: Application strategy:

items.text: Prepare a one-page cybersecurity resume.
Showcase two or three documented projects.
Practise explaining a suspicious-login or phishing investigation.
Apply to internships and graduate trainee roles.
Learn to distinguish observed evidence from assumptions in technical interviews.

blocks.label: Core foundations
blocks.text: Networking, Linux, Windows, and security principles.

blocks.label: Defensive skills
blocks.text: Log analysis, SIEM concepts, alert triage, and incident documentation.

blocks.label: Programming
blocks.text: Python scripting, log parsing, and basic automation.

blocks.label: Forensics
blocks.text: Hashing, evidence integrity, file-system artefacts, and timeline construction.

blocks.label: Portfolio
blocks.text: Three well-documented projects using authorised datasets or isolated labs.

blocks.label: Employability
blocks.text: A targeted resume, interview practice, and an internship if possible.

blocks.label: Recommended pathway
blocks.text: B.Sc. Cyber Security / Digital Forensics → networking and operating-system fundamentals → SIEM and log-analysis projects → internship → SOC Analyst L1 or Junior Security Analyst.
If the student prefers investigative work, develop a parallel digital forensics portfolio. If the student enjoys monitoring and rapid problem-solving, focus on SOC operations and incident response.

The strongest entry-level candidates demonstrate that they can investigate events methodically, distinguish evidence from assumptions, communicate findings clearly, and escalate security issues responsibly.
